title: In the Inquest Touching the Death of GRAEME JOHN HEMMING [2018]
text:
COR-07-18 
INQUEST (resumed) into the death of Graeme John Hemming   
        
1. Good afternoon.  I am sitting as coroner today,11th July 2018  to resume the 
inquest into the death of Graeme John Hemming  whose death was reported on 
5th April 2018 . The inquest was opened on 20th April 2018 when I received 
evidence  of Mr Hemming’s identity and a little information about the 
circumstances in which his body had been found. The inquest was adjourned for 
further inquiries to be made and those inquiries have now been completed.  
2. As I said at the opening of the inquest, this is an inquiry; no one is on trial, least of 
all the deceased. The inquiry is to find answers to four limited but factual 
questions: 
• Who was the person? 
• When did he die? 
• Where did he die? 
• How did he come by his death? 
3. As I have already received evidence identifying Mr Hemmming name of deceased, 
I am now seeking answers to when, where and how he died.  For this inquest, as 
in every coroner’s inquest, the question “how” is limited to finding out by what 
means Mr Hemming came by his death. The aim is to ascertain the simple facts of 
what actually happened and the inquiries are focused on the direct cause of 
death.  An inquest is not a trial and it is not a method of apportioning guilt or 
blame nor is it an opportunity to examine the broader circumstances in which 
the death occurred.  The role of the Coroner is to examine the evidence to find 
answers to the four questions.  My conclusion will form the verdict.  
4. The proceedings today are conducted under the Coroner’s Act 1988 (of England) 
as it applies in modified form in the Falkland Islands, and the Falkland Islands’ 
own Coroner’s Rules 1995. [Under rule 39 a coroner who believes that action 
should be taken to prevent the recurrence of fatalities similar to that in respect of 
which the inquest is being held may announce at the inquest that as coroner he 
or she is reporting the matter in writing to the person or authority who may have 
power to take such action and may report the matter accordingly.  Later in these 
proceedings I shall refer to making such a report.] 
5. I give notice of my intention, under rule 33 of the Coroner’s Rules 1995, to admit 
documentary evidence in the form of written statements provided by witnesses 
to the circumstances of [deceased]’s death.  This documentary evidence includes 

 
 
a report of a post mortem examination carried out on my instruction. I will be 
calling the Coroners officer inthis case who can draw on the statements  to 
provide the inquest with the evidence.[I do not intend to call  any of the expert  
witnesses to give oral evidence as the  witnesses are not resident in the Falkland 
Islands and are not able to attend this inquest   and in my opinion, their evidence 
is not likely to be disputed.    I have given notice to  family of my intention to 
admit written evidence today and no objection has been raised. The 
documentary evidence I intend to admit is as follows: 
• Statement  dated 5th April 2018of PC Zena Butler  dated 5th April 2018 who 
attended the home of Mr Hemming where he was found 
• Report 29th May 2018 of forensic pathologist Dr Littler that the cause of death 
was acute ethanol toxicity with complications of chronic ethanol misuse 
• Toxicology report  dated 14th May 2018  of Dr Paul Smith showing the levels of 
alcohol in his blood.  
 
If any person wishes to object to the admission of this documentary evidence he or 
she should make objection now.  Similarly, if a person wishes to see a copy of the 
documentary evidence he or she should say so now.   I ask any person seeking to 
object or wishing to see a copy of the documentary evidence to state how he or she 
claims to be within Rule 19 of the Coroner’s Rules.  Are there any objections or 
requests for copy documentary evidence? 
[Allow time for objection or request.  If none proceed as 6 and 7 below]  
6. There being no objections and no requests to see copy documentary evidence, I shall 
call Mr Whitby  
7. I will read the statements and report aloud and thus into the record of the inquest. 
8. In respect of Dr [ ]’s report  I shall only read out an extract although the full report 
will be kept on the court file.  This is because the report contains personal medical 
evidence that is not relevant to cause of death.  I shall restrict myself to reading 
[describe sections e.g. his conclusions]. 
9. [Read statements and extracts from autopsy report] 
10. Summary  
I shall now give a summary of my reasons for my conclusions.  I have considered 
the evidence carefully but I shall not repeat the detail from each statement.  I shall 
confine myself to what I am satisfied are the most important elements. 
i) Graeme John Hemming born 12.09.62 In London and of British nationality  
ii) He was found dead at his home.  The precise time of death and cause of death 
was unknown so it was brought to the attention of the police and then to the 
Coroner[information as to why death brought to attention of RFIP/Coroner] 

 
 
iii) He was initially discovered by his social worker mr Nathan murphy on his 
weekly appointment to see Mr Hemming.  When discovered he was sitting in 
thei lounge area of his home.  His head was slumped and he had dried blood 
on his mouth and shirt.  There were a number of empty bottles of rum in the 
home. 
iv) Although time of death is unknown and wrong to speculate He was last seen 
alive on 29th March 2018 by a neighbor. Further his last transaction was with 
the Chandlery on the morning of 29th March with delivery later that day.  It is 
likely he died nearer to the datre of 29th March than to the darte of April 5th 
when discovered.  
v) He had a history of alcohol abuse.  There is evidence of kidney impairment.   
vi) The cause of death was   
1a) -acute ethanol toxicity  
II Complications of chronic ethanol misuse
